name: Tomb of Aeons

stars.name: The Pallbearer
stars.notes: Hot white dwarf with hydrogen-rich atmosphere, surface temperature approximately 40,000 K. Faint ultraviolet glow visible from all three orbiting bodies.

planets.name: Lament
planets.notes: Tidally locked scorched rock, its day side a glassy plain fused by the star's former red giant phase. Subsurface tunnels of unknown origin riddle the night side.

planets.name: Cenotaph
planets.notes: Dead world bearing the eroded remains of monumental architecture visible from orbit. Atmosphere stripped long ago, leaving structures flash-preserved in vacuum.

planets.name: Dirgefall
planets.notes: Outermost body, a frozen husk with a thin nitrogen frost. Automated beacons of unknown origin still emit faint, repeating signals from its equatorial ridge.

anomalies.name: The Wailing Frequency
anomalies.notes: Repeating low-frequency signal on a 77.3-hour cycle. No known technological match. Signal predates human expansion by an estimated 2 billion years.

anomalies.name: The Glass Meridian
anomalies.notes: Perfectly straight vitrified line running 4,200 km across the planet's surface, far too regular to be natural. Cause unknown.

asteroid_belts.name: The Cortege
asteroid_belts.location: Between orbits of Cenotaph and Dirgefall
asteroid_belts.notes: Remnants of a fourth body that did not survive the star's red giant expansion. Contains fragments of worked metal among the natural debris.

faction_control.notes: No faction claims this system. Listed as a protected archaeological site in Exploration Guild registries, though enforcement is nonexistent.

history: Catalogued by automated survey probe in 2389, initially dismissed as an unremarkable white dwarf system until spectral analysis revealed anomalous metallic signatures on the second planet.

An Exploration Guild expedition in 2412 confirmed the presence of ruins on Cenotaph predating all known civilizations by at least 1.8 billion years, triggering a brief academic furor that faded when no artifacts could be safely extracted.
The system remains unvisited for decades at a stretch. The last recorded entry was a solo archaeologist in 2597 who filed incomplete notes before departing and never returned to the field.
description: The Tomb of Aeons orbits a dying ember of a star—The Pallbearer, a blue-white white dwarf radiating the last of its thermal reserves into the void. Three dead worlds circle it in silence: a scorched rock, a monument-scarred wasteland, and a frozen husk whispering into the dark. The system is cold, dim, and profoundly still, the kind of place where ship sensors return readings that feel like holding your breath.

Something built here, once. The ruins on Cenotaph are beyond ancient—they predate complex life on Earth by a comfortable margin. Whoever raised those structures did so when The Pallbearer was still a healthy main-sequence star, burning bright enough to warm a living world. Now the monuments stand in vacuum, their builders gone so long that even their erosion has eroded. The Glass Meridian on Lament and the signal from Dirgefall suggest the builders' reach extended across the entire system, but their purpose remains utterly opaque.

No faction bothers to claim the Tomb of Aeons. There is nothing here to extract, no strategic position to hold, no population to govern. What remains is a question etched in stone and glass and radio waves: who were they, and where did they go? The answer, if it exists, lies buried under billions of years of silence. The system waits, as it has always waited, for someone patient enough to listen.
